Applied Physics for Pre-Engineering Requirements

It is highly recommended that students considering auditing a course discuss this decision with their academic advisor and ensure that it will not disrupt the student’s progress towards a degree or negatively impact their financial aid.
Western accepts up to 90 credits, combined total, from accredited institutions, military credit, AP, IB, Challenge Exams, Experience-Based Learning Portfolio Assessments, and CLEP exam.

Total combined credit permitted under AP, IB, DSST, Challenge Exams, Experience-Based Learning Portfolio Assessments, and CLEP exams leading to credit is limited to 40 semester credits, with a maximum of 18 semester credits allowed for CLEP and a maximum of 30 credits allowed from Experience-Based Learning Portfolio Assessments.
A student who has a Cumulative GPA above a 2.0 meets this requirement.
A student will remain on academic probation as long as their semester GPA is a 2.0 or higher and their cumulative GPA is below 2.0.
At the end of a probationary semester, students with 45 or more Western credits will be suspended if their semester and cumulative GPA are below 2.0.
After a probationary period in which a student has attempted 45 or more Western credits and fails to bring their cumulative GPA to or above a 2.00, the student is suspended.
After returning from academic suspension, students with a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or higher are considered in good standing, even if their semester GPA falls below 2.0.
Students whose cumulative GPA is below 2.0 but who earn a semester GPA of 2.0 or higher will remain on academic probation and be allowed to continue enrollment.
However, students whose cumulative GPA is below 2.0 and who also earn a semester GPA below 2.0 will be academically dismissed.
Students are required to have a minimum GPA of 2.0 or higher in order to obtain an undergraduate certificate.
